answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a recurring, untransferable work bond that renews on every settlement pulse. A new identity enters as a single low-trust vertex with no inbound attestations. Only after independently verified work accumulates do peer grades act as a prism, splitting the record into quality, uniqueness, and consistency bands. Cheap clone farms fail because they cannot staff enough distinct high-quality work to light all three bands at once, so the vertex stays isolated and earns no settlement share.
